newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. okays regulatory agency consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. okays regulatory agency consolidation.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson signed legislation to consolidate and streamline the state agencies that regulate depository institutions, Wilson's office said on Sunday.

The legislation will create the Department of Financial Institutions by consolidating the licensing and supervision responsibilities of the State Banking Department, the Office of Savings and Loan, and the Credit Union and Industrial Loan regulatory programs currently housed within the state Department of Corporations.
Wilson said the bill, by Assemblyman Ted Weggeland, a Riverside, Calif., Republican, would bring about greater efficiency and more consistent application of regulatory standards.

"As the unnecessary barriers between various industries are removed, potential 'turf battles' among regulatory agencies can be avoided," said Wilson. "This also helps eliminate consumer confusion since all depository institutions will now have the same regulator."
The bill becomes effective on July 1, 1997.
